question: Ticket 266d39d56d06 says "D2 creates a published tool cairn/devices/codemother/tools/inspect_wire/ (published_by_device true) to handle wire serialization, arguing RULE 1 requires it: 'the callers sit outside codemother and RULE 1 lets them reach into her only through a published tool'", but outline 9.4.3.3.4 reads "Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"" (9.4.3.3.4 states: 'Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus... No published client tool, no fifth exception.' The outline forbids the published-tool approach the ticket proposes. The four existing published exceptions (Database 2.3.7.1.1, Librarian 2.3.7.1.2, Trouble 2.3.7.1.3, Scratch bus 2.3.7.1.4) are the allowed set. Adding inspect_wire as a fifth violates this explicit constraint.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands. 2.3.7.1 lists exactly four client tools a device publishes (Database, Librarian, Trouble, Scratch bus), and 9.4.3.3.4 says code outside CodeMother reaches build_inspector over the bus: 'No published client tool, no fifth exception' (Akien on Q#88: 'over the bus. that's what it's for?'). inspect_wire published by codemother is a fifth, so 266d's D2 is built wrong on its client side. 266d's CodeMother side stays: the inspect verb, INSPECT_JUDGES and decoding on arrival. Follow-up ticket 0c2c3f53c2be (child of 4c4addb09adb) does three things. It moves the wire codec and ask() to a plain tool, cairn/tools/inspect_wire/, which imports nothing from codemother. ask() reaches a real CodeMother process on the scratch bus, started by name by scratch_bus (exception 4). fixture() goes: the scratch CodeMother's berth, ticket and crossing roots are set by its launch environment.
